changes.after: Starter: Prepare To Be the Audience

changes.before: Makers forget how art arrives. This week's event — gallery, gig, mural walk or screening — flips you to the receiving end. What will you notice that a non-artist can't?
changes.after: An arts event — gallery, gig, mural walk or screening — lets you look as an audience member. Until an actual experience is arranged, use this as preparation. What might you notice through a maker’s eyes?
Current event route: staff check the shared slots file. Until confirmed, prepare only.

changes.before: If you missed the visit: choose from the studio event bank instead — a recorded gallery walk-through, an online collection you can browse, or a filmed local mural or maker documentary. Reviewing a recorded event still evidences Part B. Evidence photos go in your Arts Award portfolio — your event capture sheet + review (Part B complete after this cycle).
changes.after: If no actual arts experience is available: use practice material as preparation and keep that label. Staff check the current EVENT_SLOT before delivery. An online exhibition is a valid audience experience when actually undertaken. A recording or research alone remains preparation. Keep the real capture sheet and review, plus evidence that the pupil’s views were shared with at least one other person. The adviser checks all Part B requirements; this lesson does not declare completion.

changes.before: the curator line written to be SENT (we will).
changes.after: the curator line prepared to share with an agreed listener; any onward sending needs an agreed recipient and permission.

changes.before: The event is the space — off-site or visiting-artist session run to YOUR capture routes; move as your looking demands (venue rules respected).
changes.after: Use an actual arts experience when arranged, following the setting’s rules. Until then, practise your capture choices in class and label the work preparation.

changes.before: Your question from the sheet gets ASKED — to the artist, the staff, or the room. Questions are audience rights.
changes.after: Choose a question from your sheet. Ask it through an available route, or keep it ready until a person can respond. Record only a reply you actually receive.

changes.before: You ARE the audience this week — and your reviews go to the venue/artist, who asked to receive them. Real reception, both ways.
changes.after: After an actual arts experience, share your views with at least one other person and keep evidence. Staff must agree any onward contact with an artist or venue; no request to receive work is assumed.

changes.before: The curator lines from Stretch (and any volunteered) are sent to the venue. Last cohort's line changed a label height. Yours may too.
changes.after: You can choose a point you want a listener to understand. Record what was shared and any response that really happened. A change at a venue is not promised.

changes.before: your event capture sheet + review (Part B complete after this cycle).
changes.after: Your actual event capture sheet and review, plus evidence that your views were shared with at least one other person. Preparation alone does not complete Part B.
My curator line (to share with an agreed listener):

changes.before: Event logistics on the board (venue/visiting artist, times, groups, venue rules). Capture sheets on clipboards. Photo policy stated per venue.
changes.after: Open Guidance on the title slide, then Current organisation and event details. ORG_SLOT is an organisation reference; EVENT_SLOT is the event route. Check actual arrangements before delivery. Unconfirmed work stays preparation. Use capture sheets for an actual experience and follow that setting’s photo rules.

changes.before: At the event: circulate for specifics ('name the work'), guard the two-photo discipline. Back in room: reviews from sheets, not memory. Photograph sheets + reviews (Part B).
changes.after: When an actual arts experience takes place, support specific capture and follow the setting’s photo rules. Build reviews from real records. If it has not happened, label the work preparation. Keep the pupil’s review and evidence that views were shared with at least one other person.

changes.before: Collect transfer lines + curator lines — transfers feed next week; curator lines genuinely get sent.
changes.after: Collect transfer lines and the pupil’s chosen sharing point. Record real sharing with an agreed listener. Any onward sending needs an agreed recipient and permission; do not claim it happened in advance.
